memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'So I told them, "Whoever has any gold jewellery, take it off." Then they gave me the gold, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!'" - Exod 32:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This may be one of the most transparently absurd sentences in Scripture. Verse 4 has already told us plainly that Aaron shaped the calf with a tool. Now he claims it just walked out of the fire on its own.

It would be funny if it were not so sad. And if we are honest, it is not so far from our own words. "It just happened." "Things got out of hand." "I don't know how I ended up here."

Sin rarely just happens. There are choices along the way — small compromises, ignored warnings, quiet refusals to walk away. By the time we say "out came this calf," we are usually protecting ourselves from a truth we already know.

God is not fooled, and He is not shocked. The One who sees everything is also the One who came to save. Jesus did not wait for us to construct a decent account of ourselves. While we were still sinners, Christ died for us (Rom 5:8).

So there is no need to pretend before Him. He already knows how the calf got made. And He loves you enough to have died for it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you told yourself "it just happened"?
2. What small choices led to something you now regret?
3. What would it mean to bring the whole truth to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I stop pretending. You see everything, and You love me still. Thank You for the cross. Amen.
